title: Rhinoplasty: Open vs Closed, Valves and Tip Dynamics

steps.say: Complex tip work is demanding full exposure of the cartilaginous framework. An inverted-V cut across the columella joined to marginal incisions inside both rims is lifting the whole skin envelope. Complete unhindered vision is guiding precise graft placement and suture shaping.
steps.tx: **Open rhinoplasty** pairs an inverted-V **transcolumellar incision** with bilateral **marginal incisions** for complete unhindered exposure of the nasal **cartilaginous framework**. The lifted envelope reveals every cartilage. Complex tip reconstruction needs this panoramic view before grafting begins. Exposure quality is deciding graft precision in every complex case.

The image opens the nose from below with retractors showing an **inverted V incision** across the columella joined to **marginal incisions** along the rims to expose lower lateral cartilages. Wide lift reveals the full **cartilaginous framework** for precise graft work. Choose this route when complex tip shaping needs full vision rather than a hidden internal cut.
steps.say: This operative view looks up at the nose with the skin lifted back on metal retractors. A small V shaped cut crosses the central column between the nostrils and continues inside each rim. That lift bares the paired tip cartilages below. Full exposure like this guides exact graft placement when tip work is complex.

vis.alt: Open operative view of the nose with retractors showing the inverted V and marginal incisions over the tip cartilages.
vis.caption: Open nose exposure through rim incisions, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Simpler humps with good tip support are suiting a scarless internal route. Cuts hidden between or within the cartilages are reaching the dorsum without any external columellar mark. Postoperative tip swelling is settling faster because the skin envelope stays down.
steps.tx: Closed **endonasal rhinoplasty** uses **intercartilaginous** or intracartilaginous incisions hidden inside the nostril. No external **columellar scars** result, and postoperative tip **edema** stays minimal. Simpler dorsums with sound tips suit this less disruptive internal route that hides every scar. Dorsal smoothness still demands precise hump handling through the narrow corridor.

steps.say: Most nasal resistance is arising from one narrow angle deep inside the nose. The upper lateral cartilage meeting the septum beside the turbinate head is forming the internal nasal valve. An angle of only ten to fifteen degrees is governing airflow at this choke point.
steps.tx: The **internal nasal valve** bounded by **upper lateral cartilage**, **nasal septum**, inferior turbinate head, and pyriform floor is the narrowest airway cross-section. Its **10 to 15 degree** angle governs most resistance. Valve narrowing explains obstruction after otherwise neat surgery, so spreader grafts protect it routinely.

steps.say: Hump takedown is detaching the middle vault walls and risking pinched collapse. Cartilage battens placed between the dorsal septum and the upper lateral cartilages are stenting the walls apart. The middle vault is staying open instead of caving into an inverted-V deformity.
steps.tx: **Spreader grafts (Sheen)** placed between dorsal septum and **upper lateral cartilages** rebuild the **internal nasal valve** after hump reduction. They stent the middle vault and prevent **inverted-V** roof collapse. The pinched airway stays open because the grafted walls hold firmly apart.

The image looks down the dorsum with paired **spreader grafts** set between septum and **upper lateral cartilages** to hold the **internal nasal valve** open near ten to fifteen degrees. Stented walls resist pinched collapse after hump takedown. Remember grafts as the fix when middle vault narrowing threatens airflow and shape.
steps.say: This top down view shows two pale graft bars lying on either side of the central septum beneath the side wall cartilages. Arrows mark the narrow valve angle staying open with no pinched V shape above. The grafts act like spacers that keep the middle vault from caving inward after hump removal, so air still passes freely.

vis.alt: Top view of the nasal dorsum showing paired spreader grafts beside the septum holding the valve angle open.
vis.caption: Spreader grafts holding the middle vault open, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Tip position is balancing on a three-legged cartilage frame. Two lateral crura with the joined medial crura are forming the Anderson tripod that sets projection and rotation. Shortening the medial legs is dropping projection and turning the tip downward predictably.
steps.tx: The **Anderson tripod** models two **lateral crura** with conjoined **medial crura**: shortening the medial legs drops **tip projection** and rotates downward. Lengthening support pushes the tip up. Every tip manoeuvre is moving one leg of this tripod frame, so the result stays predictable.

steps.say: A weak tip is collapsing under scar contracture without internal support. A cartilage post placed between the medial crura is bracing the whole tip complex. Projection is holding steady and retracted columella is coming forward as the strut heals in.
steps.tx: A **columellar strut** graft between the **medial crura** strengthens tip support, maintains **tip projection**, and corrects columellar **retraction**. The post braces against contracture. Weak tips gain lasting structure instead of settling back down under progressive scar pressure over months. Contracture loses against cartilage every time.

steps.say: Hump resection is leaving the bony vault spread open like a pitched roof. Controlled fractures along the nasofacial groove are swinging the nasal bones inward. The open roof is closing as the bones meet the septum and dorsal lines smooth out.
steps.tx: **Lateral osteotomies** along the **nasofacial groove** narrow the widened vault and close the **open-roof deformity** after bony hump resection. The mobilized bones meet the septum. Smooth dorsal lines from radix to tip return once the mobilized roof shuts completely. Greenstick control keeps the fracture line exactly along the planned groove.

steps.say: Over-trimmed rims are buckling inward on inspiration and blocking the outer valve. Preserving at least six to eight millimetres of lateral crus width is keeping the rim stiff. Alar retraction with external collapse is avoided because the residual strip holds its curve.
steps.tx: **Cephalic trim** must leave a residual **lateral crus** rim of at least **6 to 8 mm** in width to avoid **external nasal valve** collapse with **alar retraction**. Narrower rims buckle on inspiration. The residual strip keeps its curve and holds the nostril open.

rows: At least six to eight millimetres
